info.title: API.SH: The Guardian
info.description: The The Guardian API from API.SH: public The Guardian data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.description:
One Guardian article by its link: headline, standfirst, trail text, byline and authors (profile link, picture, X handle), first-published and update times, section, pillar, type, topic tags, main image or video, and the full text as ordered blocks (paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes, inline images with caption and credit, embeds), plus the related links shown in the article, the word count, the short link and the reader comment count. Live blogs also return their latest updates (time, title, key-event and pinned flags, text) and key events. `latest=true` with `section` opens the newest article of a section.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/guardian-article

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: A theguardian.com article link (…/<section>/<yyyy>/<mon>/<dd>/<slug>), or that path alone.

parameters.name: latest
parameters.description: true opens the newest article of `section` instead of `url`.

parameters.name: section
parameters.description: With latest=true: a section or tag path as in /guardian/v1/headlines (default international).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

Reader comments on a Guardian article with replies: text, author, time, recommendations, reply-to, highlighted flag; the thread's comment count and whether it is closed. Pass `next_page` back as `page`, null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/guardian-comments

parameters.name: threads
parameters.description: Replies: up to 3 per comment (`collapsed`, default), all (`expanded`), or a flat list.

get.summary: Guardian headlines by section or tag
get.description:
The latest stories (up to about 100, newest first) of any Guardian section, topic tag, series or contributor page: headline, standfirst, link, publication time, byline, section, type (article, liveblog, video, audio, gallery), topic tags with their paths and image. Filter by keywords and since a time. With `page`, any numbered page of the listing (20 stories a page, back through the archive) instead, with `page`, `last_page`, `total` and `next_page`; on topic, series and contributor pages each story also has `trail_text`, `thumbnail`, `pillar` (News, Opinion, Sport, Arts, Lifestyle), `design`, `series`, `is_live`, `commentable`, `short_url`, `main_media` (lead image or video with caption) and `comment_count` (section fronts give headline, link, time and image). By date: `date` (one day) or `from`/`to` (up to 366 days, default the last 7 days) with `order` newest or oldest return every story published on those days (headline, standfirst, link, day, section, type, kicker, pillar, image, short link, comment count); each call returns one day (empty days included), pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor`; null after the last day. `edition` (uk, us, au, international, europe) reads that edition's own front of a section. Stories are in English (the site publishes no other language); share counts are not shown by the site. Article bodies are not returned (use /guardian/v1/article).

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/guardian-headlines

parameters.name: section
parameters.description: A section or tag path as in the site's addresses: international (default), uk, us, au, world, uk-news, us-news, politics, business, technology, science, environment, sport, football, culture, lifeandstyle, commentisfree, a topic tag such as technology/artificialintelligenceai, a series, or profile/<contributor>.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Only stories whose headline or standfirst contains all these words.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only stories published at or after this date or ISO time.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum stories (default 50, max 100).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: A page number of the listing, 1 = newest (20 stories a page). Pass `next_page` from the previous response. Without it, the latest stories are returned.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: One publication day (YYYY-MM-DD): every story of that day in the section or tag.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start of a date range (YYYY-MM-DD).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End of a date range (YYYY-MM-DD, default today).

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: With a date range: newest (default) or oldest first.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: With a date range: the `next_cursor` from the previous response.

parameters.name: edition
parameters.description: The site edition whose front of the section to read: uk, us, au, international or europe.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
